title: Inauguration of the U.P. Film Center
description: Formal inauguration of the U.P. Film Center Fine Arts Complex, featuring speeches of Imelda Marcos, awards, and recognition of leading Filipino filmmakers.
full_description: The formal inauguration of the U.P. Film Center Fine Arts Complex marked the opening of the University of the Philippines Film Center’s dedicated facilities and its establishment as a major institutional venue for film education, exhibition, production, research, and cultural activities. Imelda Romualdez-Marcos was invited to the inaugural event, while writer and filmmaker Virginia R. Moreno delivered a speech. Three young Filipino filmmakers—Lino Brocka, Ishmael Bernal, and Eddie Romero—were presented with awards during the ceremony. In lieu of the customary cornerstone, an antique jar containing a film reel and a painter’s palette was buried as the inauguration’s ceremonial foundation object. The ritual symbolized cinema’s relationship with earlier artistic traditions and expressed the idea that modern cinema could serve both as a user and preserver of older arts and of life itself. Following its inauguration, the Film Center operated as a central workshop for cinematic studies, developed the beginnings of a film research archive, and served as a showcase theater for Filipino and international cinema. The event consequently marked an important moment in the institutional establishment of film as an academic, artistic, archival, and cultural practice at the University of the Philippines.
